newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan send condolences to families of fire victims.
newsitem.headline: Annan send condolences to families of fire victims.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan offered condolences on Tuesday to the families of the victims of a disastrous fire near Mecca which killed some 200 Moslem pilgrims and injured hundreds of others.

"The secretary-general has learned with great sadness of the tragic death of almost 200 pilgrims and the injuries sustained by hundreds of others in a fire near the Holy City of Mecca," a statement issued through a U.N. spokesman said.
Annan, now on a visit to Italy, "wishes to express his sincere condolences to the families of the victims at this time of great sorrow," the spokesman said.
The secretary-general also extended sympathy to King Fahd and to the government and people of Saudi Arabia.
Later reports put the number of dead at 217 and said 1,290 pilgrims were injured when fire tore through an encampment of some 70,000 tents.
